note_en: 越来越 + adjective means "more and more" or "-er and -er": 她每天的工作也变得越来越忙 "her days are getting busier and busier." English has to repeat the comparative, but Chinese says it once with 越来越. A related pattern puts a verb in the gap, 越A越B, as in 队伍越排越长 "the line kept getting longer (the more people lined up)."
